sessions.summary: S1 LANDED on master (11cd459): 696 nodes, 269/7 against the previous 269/2. sessions.title: BoxMind does NOT publish the distance mix - the derived 40% stays derived, and it is a floor
sessions.summary: The fetch is ANSWERED NO and BoxMind is spent as a source for this question. The three-way `distance in {Long, Mid, Close}` lives on the ATOM (J21 has that DIRECT and it is correct); the published INDICATORS collapse it to TWO buckets - `Close- & Mid-Range` against long range - deliberately, because close and mid share infighting characteristics and the contrast drawn is infighter vs out-boxer. sessions.title: B's target was written in the wrong distribution - the position move is 16.7 points, not 4.1
sessions.summary: MEASUREMENT ONLY, nothing flipped. (1) THE SIZING TRAP: S4i solved 40.5% over NAMED THROWS; B is written as a POSITION move, which is STANDING occupancy. The map between them is the per-band throw density - LONG 0.703, MID 0.768, POCKET 1.568 throws per in-gate tick, so POCKET is 2.23x denser than LONG. Delivering a 40.5% named-throw LONG needs in-gate LONG occupancy to go 36.4% -> 53.1%, a 16.7-POINT move; reading the target as 4.1 points UNDERSIZES it by 4.1x. Fifth normalisation trap in six stages, caught before it produced a wrong finding. (2) THE MEN ALREADY STAND AT LONG MORE THAN THEY THROW THERE: in-gate tick occupancy is 36.4/31.7/31.9 against a named mix of 25.6/24.3/50.1 - and 69.6% of standing ticks are OUTSIDE the 1.10 m strike gate entirely. (3) INSIDE THE GATE THE 'TOO FAR - CLOSE HIM DOWN' BRANCH NEVER FIRES: 0.0% for both men, 80.8% 'too close' pooled. Whenever they are close enough to fight, both are trying to back off, so the band a beat lands in is the profile of a CROSSING and not of a chosen standoff. (4) WHY: `preferred_range` returns a SCALED distance (contested_range compares it against Moves.scaled_distance and says so; the 1.17/0.88 cuts and the Hristovski D join are in that unit) and `_run_decision` compares it against a METRE gap - and FightBeatAdapter reads it back as `range_m`. Under today's reading 37 of 37 featured athletes with a recorded reach want a standoff BEYOND the strike gate. Converting first moves A's in-gate 'in band' share 0.0% -> 32.8% and B's 32.3% -> 63.8%. (5) REACH DOMINATES the formula 4.20x over power and 6.46x over technique on the 37 real athletes with a reach - and 63 of the 100 featured athletes carry reach_cm = 0, a MISSING value the formula clamps to the 0.4 floor. (6) THE GAP IS BIMODAL: 29.6% of decision intervals move it under 1 cm, 37.8% move it further than that man's whole reachable LONG window (0.158 m for A against a p90 step of 0.629 m). (7) ONLY 62.7% of beats are scored in the band the actor was standing in at his last decision, and the drift runs INWARD.

handover.blocked_on_operator_detail: BEARING WAS RULED ON AND BUILT - OPTION B, 2026-09-15, do NOT re-ask. Kept for the record:  The operator asked how to implement bearing and said the default should be that a fighter faces his opponent ALWAYS. That is right as an intent and wrong as an implementation, and `research/S4E_BEARING_DESIGN.md` has the three options. The engine has NO facing at all - `rg -n 'facing|bearing|yaw'` over FightRealtime/FightIntent/FightFootwork/RingSpace returns ONE hit and it is the phrase 'load-bearing' in a comment. OPTION A derived (free, but turning costs nothing so cutting a man off buys nothing); OPTION B carried with a turn rate (RECOMMENDED - one authoritative number the room and both clip pipelines read, its own switch, a re-baseline); OPTION C is B plus the stance blade and an off-line penalty, which is where cutting off finally PAYS - its own slice, never folded into B. ASK WITH THOSE THREE. THE INTEGRATION IS THE POINT: a pair record already gates on DISTANCE (`min_gap_m`/`max_gap_m`) and bearing gets the SAME treatment - `authored_bearing_deg` plus a tolerance, refused by `_present_pair` exactly as an out-of-range pair already is. Higgsfield clips are one actor on their own axis, so bearing is what tells the assembler how far to rotate the root. The turn rate has NO STUDY and is measurable with the instrument already built: the shoulder-line normal in the 17 MediaPipe tracks IS the facing, so ADD A SHOULDER-LINE YAW RATE (deg/s, p50/p90) TO TASK_U109 BEFORE LAUNCHING IT - same pass, same files. handover.position_is_the_missing_key_2026_09_21:
**THE BINDING TABLE IS KEYED BY ACTION AND HAS NO POSITION, AND THAT IS THE ROOT OF THE UNBOUND RATE - not a nicety.** Raised by the operator on 2026-09-21 asking whether their BJJ simulator's vocabulary would help parse animations. It half does, and the useful half is the positional half.

All nine grapple ids are VERBS WITH NO POSITION: grapple_sweep, grapple_takedown, grapple_throw, grapple_submission_attempt, grapple_submission_finish, grapple_escape, grapple_clinch_break, grapple_control, grapple_stand_up. `grapple_sweep` does not say sweep FROM WHERE. That is exactly what refused `mma_dirty_boxing` in S6c - the action was right and the POSITION was wrong (two men upright against the fence against films of two men on the canvas), and S6c's ruling is that a wrong position is worse than no clip because absence is visible and a wrong clip is not.

The operator's fourteen split roughly ten useful / four not: POSITIONS or positional families - Guard, Top Pressure, Passing, Back Attacks, Leg Locks; TRANSITIONS - Sweeps, Scrambles, Takedowns, Submissions, Sub Defense; and NO animation meaning at all - Flexibility, Composure, Heart, Technique.

**WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY INDEX A CLIP IS A TRIPLE: position + role + action.** `half_guard / bottom / sweep` is one clip; `side_control / top / hold` is another. The table has only the third element.

**THE ENGINE ALREADY HALF-KNOWS THIS AND IT IS VESTIGIAL BELOW THE TOP FOUR.** Counting what it names across `Godot/scripts/`: `standing` 56, `clinch` 37, `mount` 28, `guard` 27, then `ground_top` 4, `ground_bottom` 4, and `side_control` 2, `cage_clinch` 2, `back_control` 2. Q114 measured 19.6% of grapple events unbound; an action-only key cannot express 'I have a clip for this, but not from here'.

**THIS BECOMES A BLOCKER AT S32 WHETHER OR NOT THE VOCABULARY IS ADOPTED**, because S32's four remaining holds - side control, guard, half guard, back control - ARE POSITIONS, not actions, and an action-keyed table cannot hold them. Recorded, deliberately not acted on at the end of S31.

handover.u117_alpha_is_fitted_2026_09_21:
**U117'S BLEND CONSTANT IS FITTED TO ONE CLIP AND NOBODY HAS TESTED WHETHER IT GENERALISES. READ THIS BEFORE AUTHORING THE OTHER FOUR HOLDS.**

The 2->3 spine split has two constants and they are NOT the same kind of number:
- **The share rule is DERIVED and safe:** rest segment lengths, Chest->UpperChest 0.139 m and UpperChest->Neck 0.155 m, giving 47%/53%. That comes off the skeleton and travels to any clip.
- **The blend is FITTED:** `alpha=0.51`, and U117's own digest says so plainly - 'linear head-gap fit: master 0.318 m -> split 0.118 m -> authored 0.216 m'. **It was chosen so the head gap of ONE clip, the S31 cage clinch, lands on its authored value.** A full split overshoots (0.118 m against 0.216 m authored) and master undershoots (0.318 m); 0.51 is the point between them that hits the target.

**WHY THAT MATTERS FOR S32.** Side control, guard, half guard and back control are different poses with different spine bends. There is no reason a constant fitted to a standing collar-and-elbow clinch is right for a man flattened out under side control, and **it has not been measured on a second clip even once.** If the next authored hold comes back with a bad head gap, suspect this before suspecting the new pose.

**THE HONEST TEST WHEN A SECOND HOLD EXISTS:** run `tools/s31_contact_probe.gd` on both holds at the same alpha. If one alpha serves both, it is a constant. If each wants its own, the blend is a symptom and the real answer is that the full split overshoots for a reason nobody has diagnosed - U117 says as much: a pure or partial split 'without skeleton-parent fix moved head the wrong way'.

**AND THE COLLAR TIE IS STILL NOT SOLVED.** U117 met the lean gate at 2% but `att_lhand_to_vic_neck` is **388%**, which is WORSE than the 337% the rejected U116 reached. That is the correct trade under the gate as written - lean first, and a run that improves the tie while the lean worsens is refused - but nobody should read 'U117 PASS' as 'the arms are fixed'. HYPOTHESIS, written up in TASK_U121: the test loads f01/f02 GLBs DIRECTLY and never calls FightWorldStage.mount, so FighterPhysique.height_scale() is never applied and its hips are in MESH UNITS while its bound is in METRES. MEASURE BEFORE CHANGING A NUMBER.

handover.session_memory_2026_09_22_S47: **S47 - THE OFFSETS WERE DERIVED, THEY WORKED, AND THAT IS HOW THE REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND.** The handover asked for derived contact offsets and named a mechanism that was WRONG, and checking it was the whole value of the stage. **`off` is ALREADY a SURFACE gap** - `evaluate` computes `capsule_gap(a,b) - off` and `capsule_gap` is `d - (r_a+r_b)` - so 'two men with 0.50 m of torso each cannot stand 0.03 m apart at the hips' is not the mechanism; 0.03 m of SURFACE gap is reachable at any stature. The real chain is one step further in: a 0.03 m pelvis surface gap puts them chest to chest at 0.29 m centre to centre, and a 0.4848 m arm sent to a neck 0.29 m away can only fold THROUGH the chest. **SO THE DERIVATION WAS BUILT AND IT LANDED: 0.0300 -> 0.1200 m, every term off the rig, a classifier that can say no (2 arms_length / 11 wrapped), the corpus read from S46's own constant map rather than copied. AND IT MOVED THE DEFECT BY 5 mm ON A 127 mm PROBLEM.** **THE PROBE IS WHAT MADE THAT A FINDING RATHER THAN A SHRUG.** A contact offset is a WANT; whether the solver reached it is a SEPARATE FACT, and reporting 'derived offsets did not help' without checking which of the two happened would have found nothing. The probe printed the stance ACHIEVED (0.1156 against a wanted 0.1200, the two men one arm apart) beside the penetration still at 0.1223 - which eliminated the stance and left only the capsules. **Print the achieved value beside the wanted one on every constraint you ever change.** **THEN THE ONE-BODY MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAD TAKEN: `neck` is 0.0% exposed on BOTH rigs**, buried 0.1610 m inside `thorax` on f02 and 0.1230 m on f01. Every neck grip in the corpus is unsatisfiable by construction and the four neck poses are four of the five worst penetrations. Cause: the thorax radius is the p80 of the Chest bone's skin and the Chest bone owns the deltoids - r=0.1909 on a 0.3054 m segment, a ball. **A THREE-SESSION HUNT (S43 offsets, S46 DOF set, S47 offsets again) WAS CHASING A DEFECT THAT WAS ON ONE BODY AND NEEDED NO SOLVER AT ALL TO SEE.** When a two-body measurement will not come right, measure ONE body first. **THE BLIND SPLIT COLLIDED AND THE COLLISION WAS REAL.** C157 (Codex) and U128 (Cursor) wrote witness and implementation from one spec with no contact and disagreed on 6 of 86 checks: 'tabular integer' read as truncation by one and `round()` by the other, differing only at 41.9 and 99.9. Settled in the module, not by editing the test to match: `100` means UNTOUCHED and `0` means GONE, so `UIKit.region_number` rounds but never ONTO a sentinel the figure has not reached, and the contract test restates that rule INDEPENDENTLY. Proof it is still a witness: both original readings now fail it at 3 failures each while the real UIKit is 86/0. **AND THE MUTANT RUN LIED FIRST.** Both mutants passed green until the `--` separator was removed: `OS.get_cmdline_args()` does NOT return user args, so `--script foo.gd -- --uikit=mutant` silently tests the REAL module. A mutant pass that catches nothing looks exactly like a mutant pass that catches everything. **Injection overrides take NO `--` separator.** **ALL EIGHT AGENTS DELIVERED IN ONE SESSION** - C157, U128, Q130, D6, G65, J37, K72, M24 - launched in the first twenty minutes and collected before the stage shipped. Grok returned G65 in ~14 minutes with 32 sources and its 60-char line matched K72's budget without either seeing the other. **THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR `--jobs 4` AFTER THE PC WENT SLOW, AND THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE SUITE** - no suite had run at all; 77 Chrome processes held 9.4 GB with 586 MB free of 31.9 GB. Answered with the measurement and took the setting anyway; by the next check it was back to 10 GB free. **When asked whether X caused the slowness, measure before agreeing.** **Q131 CAME BACK INSIDE THE SAME SESSION AND CHANGED THE NEXT STAGE.** It was launched late, on the strength of S47's finding, and it answered the one question S48 would otherwise have had to guess: the fat thorax and the live-fight overlap are one bug. **It also reported a cascade that cost it nothing to hide and everything to report** - narrowing the torso moves the bodies closer and `leg=leg` goes 7 -> 44 frames. A probe that reported only the win would have sent the next stage into that blind. **Assign the measurement that would change the next stage's plan, and do it while the finding is fresh rather than filing it for the next session.** **AND THEN THE CONTROL OVERTURNED HALF OF IT, IN THE SAME SESSION.** The operator asked whether to put Perchance on grappling. The answer was no - but the ask that WAS worth making cost one measurement and changed the next stage: `FightPoseSolver.gd` is a port of Perchance's solver, its whole rev10 source is already on disk, and running S47's own reachability test on ITS rig shows **its neck is 0.0% exposed too**, on a build that already splits the trunk three ways with slim authored radii. **Both roads S48 was written to take were closed by one cheap control.** The reason it ships anyway: it has NO all-pairs self-collision at all - eight limb points against the other body - so an unreachable neck never costs it anything. We took the cost function and applied it to a stricter comparison the source never performed. **A ported algorithm brings its blind spots with it, and the thing to measure is what the SOURCE never had to answer.** The diagnosis split in two: the thorax IS too fat (Q131 and the 0.130 m independent value both say so) AND the penetration term punishes the hold itself (a collar-tie forearm SHOULD lie on the opponent's chest). **I had already written TASK_C158 asserting neck exposure >= 5% - the control proved my own assertion false before the agent was launched.** Writing the task did not make the criterion true; measuring a second implementation is what tested it.

handover.how_skills_reach_3d:
**THE DEEP PROBLEM THIS SESSION NAMED, and four agents are evaluating it.** A skill is DATA (`technique_catalog.json`: 696 nodes with `effects`, `phases`, `range_band`, `requires`). A 3D move is a CLIP (`FightClipBinding.gd`: a path plus `length_s`). **THE TWO ARE JOINED BY NAME MATCHING AND NOTHING ELSE.**

**A technique in the catalogue has NO MOTION IDENTITY** - it says what a technique does and where it is legal, never what it LOOKS like: no limb path, no chamber, no contact surface, no arc. So the only possible bridge is guessing from the NAME, which is why **111 of Q133's 121 new bindings are marked `near`**.

**THE CANDIDATE FIX, and it is what the evaluation asks about:** Grok's G67 independently found that **120 motion ARCHETYPES cover all 534** techniques needing motion, and gave the ordered rule for when two techniques need different clips. So: **author an `archetype` field on every technique and bind clips to ARCHETYPES, not to technique ids.** 120 exact bindings instead of 534 approximate ones, and `near` stops existing as a concept. The bill is authoring 534 archetype fields - name that cost honestly before committing to it.
handover.stance_and_the_knee:
**SETTLED 2026-09-22; do not re-open without new evidence.** `FightStance.gd` implements one ruling: *'Same-stance vs open-stance flips which hand is the long hand and which body kick is free.'* Direction is the claim; the magnitudes (EDGE 0.08, DRAG 0.06) are AUTHORED, and K27 refused by name to publish a southpaw advantage figure.

Three changes landed. (1) **`family()` reads `match.limb` FIRST** - lead_hand 15 / rear_hand 34 / lead_leg 6 / rear_leg 9 - because that is an authored FACT where the marker word-lists are a guess from the name. It is also the answer to 'do elbows need their own family': **no**, an elbow is a lead or rear ARM and `muay_thai_spinning_elbow` now classifies correctly with no elbow vocabulary invented. (2) **Knees have their own family**, tested before kicks, so a knee is never called a body kick; `KICK_MARKERS` is untouched because `is_kick` is read elsewhere for kick-versus-punch questions that are not this one. (3) **A knee is freed by RANGE, not phase** - `OPEN_LINE_BANDS = [LONG, MID]` via `draw_factor_for(technique, matchup)`; an unbanded knee takes NO weight.

**Only 3 of 28 elbow nodes and 0 of 37 knee nodes carry `limb`.** Authoring it would sharpen all of this and is the named cheap win.

Close it by un-parking (operator's call) or by giving the runner an EXPECTED-RED list so a deliberate red stops counting as a failure. **Until one of those, a 'ceiling' of 8 is a number nobody trusts, and that is the real cost.**

**B. RED ON PURPOSE, TRACKING THE SAME ENGINE DEFECT - they close TOGETHER when contact lands, and must not close before (3).**
- `fight_body_overlap_test` - Q130 made it red because 5.7% of live frames genuinely overlap.
- `fighter_reachability_contract_test` - C158, the ungrippable neck, 0 of 128 approaches on both rigs.
- `fight_stage_realism_test` - **and this one had been miscategorised.** Its four failing rules are `joins_move_like_the_performance`, `joins_against_the_same_frames`, **`bodies_never_pass_through`** and `the_fist_reaches_its_target`. The third is the SAME defect as `fight_body_overlap`, measured differently. It is not a separate mystery and it is not a small bug.

**C. SMALL AND FIXABLE NOW, and nobody had read them (2).**
- `athlete_development_test`, 2 failures: *'migrate_athlete's proficiency seed is not the deterministic stat average'* and *'boxing_jab did not learn once equipment was supplied: result already_learned'*. Ordinary logic bugs.
- `weight_cut_test`, 2 failures: *'a 13% cut stops at 11%, misses by a little'* reports **Missed weight by 13.5 kg**. A 13.5 kg miss described as 'by a little' is ARITHMETIC, not tuning. Read it before touching a constant.

**D. A PRODUCT QUESTION WEARING A TEST'S CLOTHES (1).**
- `fight_scoring_test`: *'a clean uchi-mata carries enough magnitude to be an ippon (19 >= 22)'*. The throw scores 19 against a threshold of 22. **That is not a bug - it asks whether a perfectly executed uchi-mata should be an ippon**, which is a judo rules decision and the operator's, not a number to nudge. Its other two failures follow from the same call.

**ORDER: A first.** It is the cheapest and it is what makes the ceiling mean something. Then C. B closes with the stage work. D needs the operator.
handover.long_running_agent_tasks_2026_09_22: **AGENTS RUN LONG-RUNNING TASKS AND ARE CHECKED EVERY SESSION (operator, 2026-09-22, VERBATIM: 'agents need to work 24/7 when they are green on opsboard give long term tasks and keep checking on them on every new session how the progress and improve the product or whaever tasks you assign them').** THIS CHANGES THE SHAPE OF AN ASSIGNMENT. Until now every task was a one-shot with a gate, delivered once and closed - which is why the board shows ~90 tasks as OPEN that are really finished, and why every agent sat idle between sessions while the operator looked at placeholder art. WHERE IT GOT TO. The operator's idea was to beat the one-body limit by asking for one man plus an INANIMATE ground-and-pound dummy. RTMDet+RTMPose (`Tools/footage/track_pairs_rtm.py`, rtmlib+onnxruntime, both installed) gets **two or more on 100%** of the same frames. They are COMPLEMENTS: RTMPose is 2D pixels, MediaPipe gives world landmarks in METRES which is what the 98,136-frame corpus and retargeting need. Feeding RTMDet's box to MediaPipe as a crop takes the bottom man 0% -> 55% WITH metres.

**THE CAMERA WORK ITSELF.** The operator asked whether an orbiting/drone camera in the prompt would capture the action from several directions. My reading, put to the agents for challenge: **right for REAL capture, wrong for GENERATED video - you cannot triangulate a hallucination.** Multi-view 3D needs geometrically consistent views of a scene that exists; a diffusion model gives views that merely look consistent. A moving camera also makes the monocular case harder because camera motion must be solved before subject motion can be separated from it. **What a moving camera IS good for here: several FIXED angles of the same action as a validation set** (C137's rule - a pair that reads as contact from one angle and as two men in separate rooms from another is FRAMED, not solved), and it is the gold standard the moment we film anything ourselves.

But the gap between our room and a AAA fight game is mostly NOT shader fidelity. In order: (1) ANIMATION, by a mile the biggest tell; (2) CAMERA AND LIGHTING, the cheapest large win, and G74 already delivered the spec - *'the grey-void killer is the intensity split'*, bright canvas against a dark room, key from an overhead truss at 3200 K, plus a camera table with real heights and lens angles; (3) CHARACTER ASSETS - ours are Tripo meshes at arbitrary scale against a bar of scanned humans with 4K PBR, skin subsurface scattering, sweat and blend shapes. **Godot 4 Forward+ is not the ceiling** - it does PBR, SSS, real-time GI, volumetrics, bloom, DOF, motion blur, grain and a physically-based camera. Content and craft are the limit, which is consistent with the recorded engine decision. **HIGHEST VALUE SINGLE MOVE: the post-processing and lighting pass.** Days of work, no new assets, and it is the difference between placeholder primitives in a grey void and a televised fight.
handover.character_roster_r152_widened_2026_09_23:
**R152 IS WIDENED, AND THIS IS A NEXT-SESSION JOB THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR.** He said of AAA character quality: *'am sure there are tools that can do that without real humans'*. He is right and I had framed it wrongly as scanning.

**THE ARGUMENT THAT MATTERS IS NOT FIDELITY, IT IS CONSISTENCY.** Our fighters come from Tripo and every one is a ONE-OFF: arbitrary scale (only `FighterPhysique.height_scale()` makes them metres), no shared topology, no blend shapes. Each new fighter is a bespoke retarget problem. A generator gives twelve fighters on ONE skeleton and ONE topology, so one animation set drives all of them, one skin shader serves all of them, and body variety becomes a slider instead of a new asset pipeline. That is worth more than any single character looking better.

**CHARACTER CREATOR 4 (Reallusion) is the leading candidate.** Its SkinGen is literally the layered skin system - subsurface, sweat, wetness, bruising, blood, dirt as stackable layers. Body morph sliders give weight classes, which is R152's original question. Exports FBX/glTF with blend shapes, engine-agnostic. **AND WE ALREADY HOLD THE LICENCE FACT**: R142 records *'Reallusion's Standard License since 2025-08-01 allows export'*.

**METAHUMAN IS FLAGGED, NOT RECOMMENDED.** Higher fidelity, free, and UE 5.8 is already on this PC so testing the export path costs only time - but the licence historically tied MetaHuman assets to Unreal and I do not know the current terms well enough to call it safe for a Godot game. **VERIFY THE LICENCE BEFORE ANY WORK**, and do not guess at it.

Others: Daz Genesis 9 (cheapest, huge morph library, but games need the Interactive Licence at extra per-character cost); Texturing.xyz for pore-level skin micro-detail; Substance 3D Painter/Sampler for sweat and damage layers if not using SkinGen.

Fold this into R152 rather than spawning a fourth parallel investigation - the operator agreed to that framing.

detail.title: Treatments for injured parts - the management feature the injury model is already waiting for
detail.summary: OPERATOR ASKED FOR THIS ON 2026-09-17 AND THE SLOT IS BOOKED: immediately after S6. It is cheap because the foundation is built and idle. `Injury.gd` already models 8 type ids over 6 regions with severity and discipline families, cited medical rules (BBBoC 28-day facial fracture, ARP no-sparring window, laceration 14-60 days), `train_weeks`/`compete_weeks`/`hold_weeks`, `clearance_flags` (physician / specialist / ophthalmologist), and a computed `treatment_path` of `surgical` or `conservative`. **`treatment_path` is read by exactly one thing and it is a word** - `InjuryWords.gd:148` turns it into display text. Nothing charges for a treatment, nothing shortens a hold, the player never chooses. Also already on disk and unexploited: `GameState._advance_injuries` (the weekly pass), `get_recovery_options` / `assign_recovery_station` (stations exist), `enforce_pre_fight_medicals`, `InjuryHistory`, `InjuryPhase`, `RecoveryWords`. The feature is the PLAYER'S DECISION on top of all of it: choose a treatment, pay for it, and have it move the hold - with the clearance flags as the gate, so a surgical path on a severity-3 fracture cannot be bought out of. OPEN WITH 2-3 OPTIONS AND WAIT FOR THE GO; the slot is decided, the design is not. Zero asset dependency, which is why it is the track that keeps moving while clip work waits on a purchase.

deferred.title: Torso -> strength/posture, arms -> punch power and grappling, and scripted ground exchanges with escapes

detail.origin: Operator, 2026-09-18, filed explicitly as a NOTE FOR FUTURE ADD, not a greenlit stage.
detail.summary: Three ideas in one message, and reading the code turned them into TWO pieces of work plus one countable question. **(1) AND (2) ARE THE SAME JOB AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS S16.** Legwork -> footwork was cheap because the strand ALREADY existed. It does not for these: `technique_catalog.json` declares SEVEN attributes - power, technique, speed, defense, conditioning, fight_iq, grapple - and `AthleteDevelopment._strand_for_attribute:860` maps only THREE of them (speed->footwork, conditioning->conditioning, technique->technique). **`power`, `defense`, `grapple` and `fight_iq` return "" - no strand at all.** Torso->strength/posture and arms->punch-power both want `power`; "how it applies in grappling and wrestling exchanges" wants `grapple`. So the work is: add the missing strands, then the equipment and the consumers. **THE TRAP, AND IT IS A SILENT ONE:** `_strand_for_technique:851` returns the FIRST required attribute that maps to a strand. A technique requiring {power 40, technique 38} logs to `technique` TODAY because power maps to nothing; the moment power gets a strand the same technique logs somewhere else. Adding strands RETROSPECTIVELY REDIRECTS existing saves' training ledgers. Decide the precedence order deliberately and write a migration, or the change is invisible and wrong. **(3) SCRIPTED GROUND EXCHANGES - AND THE OPERATOR'S OWN QUESTION IS ANSWERABLE, SO HERE IS THE ANSWER.** "How many possible scenarios exist for each technique?" Counted off the catalogue's 452 moves: by ROLE there are **108 takedowns, 52 submissions, 26 control, 36 setup, 26 counter, 9 transition and SIX escapes.** By phase: clinch 114, ground 53, ground_top 37, ground_bottom 33, scramble 5. **The catalogue is rich in ways to GET into a position and nearly empty on ways OUT of one** - six escape-role entries against fifty-two submissions. So scripting ground combat with real escape options is mostly an AUTHORING job on the escape side before it is a scripting job, and that is the number that sizes it. (Do not confuse this with the '80 submission/escape/reversal/sweep sites' already on record - those are CODE sites in FightMoves/FightRealtime/FightSimulation, not catalogue entries.) **IT DOES NOT REOPEN THE PARKED ITEM.** The operator parked GRAPPLING ANIMATION on 2026-09-14 ("Leave grappling for later"); this is the simulation's decision tree, which needs no film. Keep them apart when this is picked up.
detail.sequence_note: Nothing here is scheduled. The live queue is S14 -> S15 -> R145 -> S16 and this sits behind all four. If it is picked up, the strand work (1+2) and the ground exchange work (3) are separate stages - one touches training and saves, the other touches the sim.

deferred.title: The phone button that starts this app - MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT, it needs an exe rebuild
deferred.detail: Operator 2026-09-20: 'can you make opsboard so that i can launch this app from there'. IT EXISTS. Tools/opsboard has POST /api/launch, a button per target, and a `claude` target in AgentComms/launch_targets.json. GET /api/launch resolves each target BEFORE it is pressed, so a moved app shows not-ready on the phone with every path it searched. The README's own closing line is the workflow: tap the button, then type /remote-control in the prompt box to drive the PC from the phone. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: the FROZEN .exe must be rebuilt for a target to appear, and that same stale exe is the one still truncating roster notes to 200 chars (feedback_ops_board_truncates_roster_notes). So this is a REBUILD plus a verification from the phone, not new code. Verify with `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/launch` first - if `claude` is listed and ready, only the exe is stale. DO NOT add a path or args parameter to the endpoint: the board binds 0.0.0.0 with NO authentication, so an endpoint that ran what it was told would be a remote shell for anything else on the Wi-Fi. Adding a target is a commit, deliberately.

deferred.title: Turning the PC on from the phone - the board CANNOT do this, by construction
deferred.detail: Operator 2026-09-20: 'and also turn on the pc from there'. THE OPS BOARD CAN NEVER DO IT: the board runs ON the PC, so if the PC is off the board is off. The only mechanism is WAKE-ON-LAN - a magic packet from something else on the LAN - and it needs three things, of which two are the operator's: (1) WoL enabled in BIOS/UEFI - OPERATOR ONLY, nobody else can reach that screen; (2) the NIC's 'Wake on Magic Packet' and 'Allow this device to wake the computer' enabled in Windows - Claude can read this with `Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement` and it is a system setting, so CHANGING it is the operator's call; (3) a SENDER that stays powered - the phone on the same Wi-Fi (a shortcut or a tiny page), or the router if it supports scheduled WoL. A cheap always-on device is the fallback. ALSO CHECK: Windows Fast Startup often breaks WoL from full shutdown, and many boards only wake from S3/S5 with the right setting - so the first measurement is which sleep state the operator actually leaves it in. Start by MEASURING, not by building: report what the NIC and current power config already allow, then give the operator the one or two switches they have to flip.

objective.text: Your objective is to finish the agreed FightCamp release. At every session start, read the project objective, settled decisions, and current assigned task. Resume from the recorded next action. Do not create a new roadmap or reopen accepted decisions without new evidence. If a change would alter agreed scope or invalidate completed work, explain the evidence and obtain approval before making that change. Continue routine implementation and fixes autonomously. Judge progress by verified playable milestones. Before ending, record the working commit, evidence, remaining work, and exact next action in the existing handoff system.
objective.where: settled decisions: research/DECISION_LEDGER.md + AgentComms/route_decisions.json (ROUTE STATUS) + CLAUDE.md rulings; current task: roadmap `now`; next action: roadmap `now.next_action`; handoff: roadmap `now` + `handover` + the stage digest.

release.definition: The release is THE WHOLE GAME, not the demo (operator 2026-09-28: 'release is not the demo, its the whole fucking game'). Scope = the phase-0 product sheet (S75, https://claude.ai/artifact/JJHo56fezkGGyVyJ4fHdjn, followed as recommended, NOT yet signed off): the most authentic fight-night management sim on Steam (Windows 10/11, keyboard+mouse); you run a combat-sports gym from a debutant's first club show to a title; three pillars - the fight is real (sourced stats, watch in 3D or sim, same result), you run the gym (sign, train, book, camp, corner, purse), it tells you why. Early Access $19.99 with v1 = stand-up (boxing, kickboxing, Muay Thai); first major update = MMA + grappling; 1.0 at $24.99; other rulesets frozen behind a switch. Not in v1: licensed athletes/leagues, multiplayer, consoles, a fighter-controlled action mode.
release.done_means: every stage A-E DONE with player-flow evidence from the exported build on disk (flow_evidence); a test, render tool or isolated demo is never 'integrated and finished'.
release.road: THE ROAD IS `stages` (A-E) - the ops board's roadmap. No second list (operator 2026-09-28: 'why you ignore the roadmap in the opsboard?'). After E (Early Access) the product sheet's first major update (MMA + grappling) and 1.0 follow.

plan._rule: THE OPS BOARD'S MAIN PAGE READS THIS (S157, operator: 'a detailed roadmap showing what is being worked, what is next, who agents are scheduled for what and who are running'). Plain words, no task jargon in titles. 'Running' is NOT listed here - the board derives it from live_runs.json (status running). Update this block at every landing, launch and handover. S164: the next session's first 15 minutes are an AGENT SWEEP (CLAUDE.md section 3) - `ship` refuses without a delegated run today.
plan.goal: MECHANICS FIRST (operator S422: 'ok prepare next session with your recommendations'): the seven mechanics the critics and you chose in S402 get built before more menu polish. Each mechanic starts with a DESIGN MAP (operator Q-173: 'what the player decides exactly and where does that happening ? which screens ? have you mapped the whole design for the mechanism ?'): the decision, the screen, what it changes, the numbers; your OK; then the build. Menus change only when a mechanic needs them. One playable .exe a week, judged by you.
